ca_mel_s_diner.blurb: Mel's Diner is a small desert crag in the Lost Horse part of Joshua Tree National Park, at roughly 4,100 feet. Nearly all of its two dozen routes are crack climbs protected with trad gear, plus a few set up for top-roping. Difficulty starts around 5.8 and reaches into the 5.11s, with the largest group at 5.10, so it suits climbers who are already comfortable on steep, sustained jamming. The granodiorite is clean, and the cliff is stepped, with a lower tier and higher ledges to either side of the central crack pair. It is quiet compared with the park's famous walls, and some shade makes it a reasonable pick for a warm day.

ca_oser_wall.blurb: Oser Wall is a high-elevation crag in Pine Creek Canyon above Bishop, near 7,700 feet in the Eastern Sierra. Its two dozen routes are split between trad and bolted sport, with grades from 5.8 into the low 5.13s and the heaviest concentration in the 5.11s. The draw is thin, precise slab climbing on granite, along with a separate bolted arete and newer trad lines that call for a full rack. Footwork matters more than strength here, so it is a committing, technical stop rather than a beginner crag. The walk in finishes with loose talus and scree, so move carefully.
ca_oser_wall.approach: Follow the canyon upstream beyond the Planetarium Wall for roughly a quarter of an hour. Scramble over a short rise of talus and scree, cross a dip, then climb again; the wall is on your left, recognizable by its smooth bolted slab.

ca_jaime_s_rock.blurb: Jaime's Rock sits in the Indian Cove section of Joshua Tree National Park, close to Group Campsite 1 and northwest of Pixie Rock, at about 3,150 feet. The 24 routes are mostly trad, with a good number of bolted lines and a single top-rope. Grades start at the very easiest end of the 5th-class scale and climb to 5.10, with nothing harder, which makes it a friendly place for newer leaders and for mixed parties wanting a range of difficulties on one small formation. The rock is monzogranite, and the setting is open desert with little tree cover.

ca_west_wall.blurb: The West Wall is the section of Lover's Leap's Main Formation nearest the campground, a granite cliff in the Sierra Nevada near Lake Tahoe. Almost every one of its two dozen routes is trad, with just a couple of bolted lines, and many are multi-pitch. Grades run from 5.7 to the low 5.12s, though most sit between 5.9 and 5.10. The rock is vertical granite split by cracks and crossed by horizontal dikes, which supply rests and handholds and make the climbing easier than the steepness suggests. The area as a whole can be busy on summer weekends.

ca_paul_s_backyard.blurb: Paul's Backyard is a short granite cliff in the northern Alabama Hills outside Lone Pine, and it is the first stop in the Paul's Paradise cluster. A small pinnacle stands in front of the wall. Most of the 24 routes are bolted, with a handful of trad lines, and the grades lean gentle: a few scrambly low-5th-class lines, a solid group from 5.6 to 5.9, and some 5.10s at the top end. The setting is open high desert at around 4,700 feet with big Sierra and Owens Valley views, which makes it a pleasant, low-pressure place for beginners and anyone warming up.

ca_gotham_city.blurb: Gotham City is a popular wall in the Upper Gorge of the Owens River Gorge, a short drive from Bishop at about 5,700 feet. Most of its 24 routes are bolted sport climbs, with a few trad lines, on the hard volcanic tuff the gorge is known for. Grades start near 5.9 and reach the low 5.13s, with most routes between 5.10 and 5.12, so it rewards climbers already comfortable at 5.11 and up. Expect technical faces plus some corner and crack systems. Mornings here are shady, and the sun takes over through the afternoon.

ca_feudal_wall_left_side.blurb: The left side of Feudal Wall is in the Indian Cove area of Joshua Tree National Park, at about 3,100 feet. Of the 24 routes, most are trad, with a few bolted lines and a couple of top-ropes. The wall offers plenty of easy to moderate cracks alongside a smaller number of tougher face climbs, so grades span the lowest 5th-class range up to the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with the largest group at 5.10. It is a common place for beginner classes. The routes mostly face south and get steady sun through the middle of the day, with no tree cover, so it is best in cooler weather.

ca_upper_irish_boulders.blurb: Upper Irish Boulders is a compact bouldering spot on Conejo Mountain near Thousand Oaks, tucked just below a powerline corridor. It holds about two dozen problems on solid stone, ranging from the easiest vertical ones through V7. Roughly half are V0 or V1, with a smaller group of V3 to V5 problems, so it works well for newer boulderers as well as a short session for stronger ones. The hillside faces away from the brightest sun and the corridor gives shade, which stretches the comfortable season. Poison oak is common, and the landings can be uneven, so bring pads and watch your footing.
